Marco: saw a reproducible tail spike after the weekend burst test — p95 ~180ms (ok) but p99 jumped to ~1.2s for a subset of requests.
Marco: looks correlated with big bursts to a single model family; reproducer attached in dashboard (link: https://dash.internal/r/abc123)
Sam: is this during scale-up or after? cold starts?\nMarco: it's during scale-up window — we see the first few batches hit a slow kernel path and lots of KV cache misses. timeline:
Marco: 00:00 burst starts -> 00:02 autoscaler kicks -> 00:03 nodes register -> 00:04 traffic routed -> p99 spikes for ~45s
Priya: can you paste the kernel selection logs? wondering if kernel fallback is triggered by microbatch size mismatch.
Marco: snippet:
```
[2026-02-18T09:02:14Z] kernel_selector: preferred=fastpath_v2, selected=compat_single_precision, reason=batch_size=1
[2026-02-18T09:02:15Z] kv_cache: miss key=usr:token:xyz, action=load_from_storage, latency=430ms
[2026-02-18T09:02:16Z] fastpath_v2: skipped, qsize=0, seq_len=512
```
Marco: TL;DR: many single-request microbatches chose compat kernel (no vectorized fastpath) and also warmed KV from cold storage causing tail.
Elena: autoscaler isn't the only culprit — we have routing hysteresis set to route new connections to newly-registered nodes immediately. That's intended for throughput but hurts steady-state tail during scale-up.
Sam: so two antagonistic effects: (1) routing to new nodes with cold KV + fallback kernel; (2) microbatch size distribution is skewed to 1 so we miss fastpath which prefers batched invocations.
Priya: interesting — when we ramp, latency-sensitive requests are thinly spread so microbatcher never accumulates enough tokens to hit fastpath. Suggest experiment: buffer-window=20ms vs 50ms for microbatcher to see p99 improvement.
Marco: ran a quick sim: buffer=50ms reduces p99 from 1.2s -> ~360ms but increases p95 by ~20ms.
Elena: tradeoff is expected — we need an SLO-aware knob: when under burst mode, increase buffer slightly up to Xms, but only for premium routes.
Sam: and we should avoid full KV eviction during bursts — current LRU TTL is 10m and our prewarm policy only fires on node join, not on routing. Idea: proactive prewarm on scale intent (pre-attach warmers during scale decision).
Priya: also noticed kernel_selector uses a throughput heuristic that picks fastpath only if expected microbatch >=4. Maybe adjust threshold for warm nodes.
Marco: filed a short perf regression: https://issues.internal/RI-4521
deploy-bot: deployment 2026-02-18T09:05:00Z started: infra/change/fastpath-telemetry
Sam: proposal for immediate experiment (safe, A/B):
- A: increase microbatch buffer from 20ms -> 50ms on canary for 10% traffic (owner: Priya)
- B: change autoscaler prewarm to call kv-prefetch job when decision > 2 nodes (owner: Elena)
- C: lower fastpath threshold from 4->2 for canary nodes only (owner: Marco)
Priya: I can run A today and attach p95/p99 heatmap. I'll set alert if p95 degrades > 50ms.
Elena: I'll prototype B as a k8s job triggered by scaler decisions, with backoff to avoid thrash.
Marco: Marco -> will handle C and add telemetry to see when fastpath is actually used (per-model, per-seq).
Sam: timeline? Priya: A in 2–3 hours, Elena: B PR tomorrow, Marco: C after telemetry merged.
Sam: next check-in in #eng-runtime tomorrow 10am. If A reduces p99 without hurting p95 too much we can roll.
Priya: added link to quick dashboard view: https://dash.internal/r/abc123?view=burst_experiment
Marco: thanks y'all. long term: think about combining prewarm + SLO-aware batching + kernel threshold per-traffic-class.
Sam: :thumbsup:
Marco: tagging ops for capacity note: @ops-team please be aware burst prewarm may require short-term headroom.
